symmetric_powers.excerpt: The compact Lean proof of RH and Dirichlet GRH combines a comparison of covolumes of theta lifts with a one-sided Mellin--Landau detector. We prove an extension of the analytic detector using a nonnegative Frobenius deficit, a fixed multiplicative finite difference, and a known abelian baseline. The difference removes an unknown centering constant, reverses the real-pole sign correctly, and allows an averaged positive-part bound in place of pointwise control. An optimal nonnegative lift of the deficit modulo abelian class functions is given for arbitrary permutation representations. For $S_4$, two Frobenius classes suffice and are necessary among detectors with strictly negative nonabelian Fourier coefficients. Two low-degree subfields realize the detector without requiring unknown Artin holomorphy. A particularly explicit target is Ramanujan's discriminant form $\Delta(q)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}=\sum_{n\ge1}\tau(n)q^n$. In unitary normalization $t(p)=\tau(p)/p^{11/2}$, $d=2$ and Deligne's theorem \cite{deligne} bounds $|t(p)|\le2$. For each symmetric power $r\ge1$ of this non-CM level-one form, automorphy and cuspidality are established by Newton--Thorne \cite{nt}. Its normalized Satake parameters are $\alpha_p^{r-2j}$, $0\le j\le r$, where $|\alpha_p|=1$ and $\alpha_p+\alpha_p^{-1}=t(p)$. Thus $d=r+1$, $t_r(p)=\sum_{j=0}^r\alpha_p^{r-2j}$ is real and $|t_r(p)|\le r+1$. Equivalently $t_r(p)=U_r(t(p)/2)$, the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind. For each fixed $r$, the detector with $w=r+1-t_r(p)$ is a precise nonnegative target for the symmetric-power RH, still beyond Dirichlet GRH. An unmodified rank-two p-adic Tate module of an elliptic curve cannot satisfy these assumptions. Its determinant is cyclotomic, which is trivial on inertia at places away from p. Therefore a scalar inertia action zeta I_2 has determinant zeta^2=1, so zeta^2-1=0 is not a unit. This is an elementary exact obstruction, independent of any unresolved conjecture. The same obstruction applies to Tate twists and duals, whose determinants remain unramified away from p.
